objective: Determine whether qualified data-center and large-load development professionals will pay for a bounded cross-source review that exposes contradictory, stale, missing, or uncertain evidence across power/interconnection, zoning/permitting, regulatory, and community constraints before expert review.

market_learning.finding: Generic power-first site screening is already competitive. Current 2026 evidence shows local approval, zoning, permitting, regulatory posture, and community opposition can be as decisive as power availability.
market_learning.product_narrowing: Do not compete as another generic site-selection or engineering tool. Test a source-linked contradiction/risk review layer that complements existing site-selection workflows.

bounded_pilot.name: Site Risk & Contradiction Review — One Site
explicit_non_capabilities: no autonomous land, contract, capital, or supplier decision

target_roles: Utility large-load planning or economic-development representative
Infrastructure-focused real estate or development advisor
questions: How often do power/interconnection findings conflict with zoning, permitting, regulatory, community, or other site evidence?
How is contradictory or stale site evidence reconciled today?
What does a missed contradiction cost in staff time, consultant spend, option diligence, or schedule?
Would a source-linked contradiction/risk packet before expert review save meaningful time?
Who owns budget for this diligence?
Would you pay $99 to test this on one real site? Why or why not?
What missing capability would prevent a paid pilot?

success_thresholds.recurring_problem: At least 2 of 3 report repeated/material contradiction, staleness, missing-evidence, or cross-domain reconciliation work.
success_thresholds.clear_cost_or_delay: At least 2 identify concrete labor, consultant, delay, diligence, or coordination cost.
success_thresholds.budget_signal: At least 1 identifies a real budget owner or paid substitute.
success_thresholds.willingness_to_pay: At least 1 unrelated qualified respondent pays $99 for the bounded pilot or gives explicit written intent to pay contingent on a specific legally/safely buildable missing capability.
success_thresholds.scope_fit: No majority requirement for regulated engineering/legal conclusions, utility approval, or prohibited consequential action.

failure_conditions: No positive willingness-to-pay signal after 10 qualified outreach responses/conversations.
Existing tools solve contradiction reconciliation with little friction.
Value depends primarily on proprietary data JakeAI cannot lawfully/economically access.
Buyers require regulated engineering or legal conclusions.
No qualified respondent identifies budget, cost, or willingness to pay.

routing.PASS: Send attributable buyer evidence to Build Authorization Gate; construction remains disabled until technical/security/legal/liability requirements are attached.
routing.HOLD: Refine scope or gather additional buyer evidence without building the full product.
routing.REJECT: Archive candidate unless materially new buyer evidence appears.

notes: Public market research supports problem existence but never counts as willingness-to-pay validation. Only attributable responses from real qualified roles count toward the buyer gate.
